learning_outcomes.text: Definition of specific elements: plastic deformation mechanism, plasticity hypotheses, schematization of material behavior in the plastic domain, plastic hinge
Calculation of displacements in the plastic domain
Use of calculation beyond the elastic limit for different stress states
Has the capacity for logical structuring, correct explanation and interpretation of results, and application of analysis and strength calculation methods
Has the capacity to investigate, design and solve calculation problems in the plastic domain of bodies and structures, under different stress states

Develops professional projects using established principles and methods in mechanical engineering based on selecting, combining, and utilizing knowledge, principles, and methods from the plastic domain
Application of knowledge necessary for identifying and analyzing mechanical phenomena and understanding the effects produced on bodies by external actions
Performs efficient teamwork and has the readiness to self-regulate behavior in relation to others on an empathetic basis
Respects ethical principles, norms, and values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks
Integrates into the work group and applies effective relationship and teamwork techniques in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels
Continuously informs and documents themselves in their field of activity by adequately using efficient learning methods and techniques
Identifies objectives to be achieved, available resources, stages, and work times
Has an open, sincere, cooperative, receptive attitude in relating and communicating within the team

syllabus_topics: Plastic deformation mechanism. Plasticity hypotheses. Schematization of material behavior in the plastic domain. Plasticity criteria. Residual stresses in elasto-plastically stressed bars.

Calculation in the plastic domain under tension and compression. Generalities. Calculation in the elasto-plastic domain of statically determinate systems. Calculation of residual stresses under tension-compression in the elasto-plastic domain of statically indeterminate systems.
Calculation in the elasto-plastic domain under torsion. Calculation of ultimate moment. Calculation of residual stresses under torsion.

Calculation under bending in the elasto-plastic domain. Generalities. Calculation of straight bars with a cross-section having two axes of symmetry. Calculation under pure symmetric bending of straight bars with a cross-section having one axis of symmetry. Formation of plastic hinges. Calculation of displacements in the plastic domain. Calculation in the plastic domain of statically indeterminate systems. Calculation of residual stresses under bending in the elasto-plastic domain.
Stresses in the elasto-plastic domain of thick-walled tubes. General considerations. Tubes stressed with internal pressure. Autofrettage (complete, partial) of tubes.
Calculation in the plastic domain. Plasticity criteria.
Calculation beyond the elastic limit of axially loaded systems.
Calculation in the elasto-plastic domain of straight bars with circular cross-section subjected to torsion.
Calculation in the elasto-plastic domain of beams subjected to bending. Formation of plastic hinges. Calculation of displacements in the plastic domain.
Calculation in the elasto-plastic domain of beams subjected to bending. Determination of residual stresses.
Calculation in the elasto-plastic domain of thick-walled tubes. Autofrettage of tubes.
teaching_methods: Descriptions using diagrams and relations written on the board
Presentation of calculation methods and relations
assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Grades will be awarded as integers from 1 to 10. A minimum grade of 5 is required for both assessment activities (exam and project) to pass the course and receive the corresponding study credits.
